name: Prize crossword No 26,316
preamble: All solutions are wholly or partly 8, which is unclued

clue.text: Old South American artist hosts writer privately

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the Incas were the old ruling people of Peru
the writer of the clue refers to themself as me
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist

explanation.surface: A Peruvian painter of old quietly entertains an author behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: INCA and RA are joined first, and that pair hosts ME between them. RA stands for Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase describes a hearing held in a judge's private chambers, away from the public.

clue.text: Cut power escaping from exhaust

indicators.note: whatever escapes gets out and is gone, so a letter leaves the word

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for power
to exhaust a supply is to use it up

explanation.surface: Someone shuts off the electricity that was leaking out of an exhaust pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' looks like a car part but is the verb meaning use up; take its P away and DEPLETE becomes DELETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut text from a document is to remove or erase it, the editing sense of the verb.

clue.text: Row during late duke's set

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls within it, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: dec. is the abbreviation for deceased
a row of things is a line
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A quarrel broke out while the late duke was being filmed on set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but means a line here; 'set' looks like a noun but is the past tense of the sun going down.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun is said to decline as it sinks towards the horizon, so having set it has declined.

clue.text: He believes in one being sweaty around noon

indicators.note: one thing placed around another wraps it, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: sweaty skin is damp
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Someone is convinced that a person can get sweaty when the midday sun beats down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One being sweaty' reads as a single sweating person, but 'one being' closes the definition and the wordplay starts at 'sweaty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monism is the philosophical doctrine that all reality is a single substance, so its follower holds there is only one fundamental existence.

clue.text: Mount watch in case

blocks.note: first meaning: a horse bred and ridden for fox hunting
second meaning: a pocket watch whose face is protected by a hinged metal lid

explanation.surface: Climb up and keep a lookout, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount watch' reads like setting a guard, but each half is a separate meaning; the second ties in with the timekeeper theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sturdy riding horse used in the hunting field and a pocket timepiece with a protective cover.

clue.text: Mingling with these beauties, Ali could be hilarious

indicators.note: the clue says these letters mix with others to make a word, so we work back by taking those others out
what could be something else is only a possible rearrangement of it

blocks.note: taken as written: the whole mixture
taken as written: the letters to remove from it

explanation.surface: Muhammad Ali surrounded by glamorous women might find the whole thing hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a subtractive anagram: the answer plus ALI is an anagram of HILARIOUS, so remove A, L and I from it and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Houris are the beautiful maidens said in Islamic tradition to await the faithful in paradise.

clue.text: Assist business to mail packages

indicators.note: to package goods is to wrap them up, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to mail a letter is to send it
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A courier firm helps a company post its parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packages' looks like a noun for parcels but is the verb meaning wraps up.
explanation.definitionFit: To second someone is to back or support them, as when seconding a motion or acting as a duellist's helper.

clue.text: Rushdie’s eloquent about this source of power

indicators.note: one thing is about another when it lies around it, so the clue words surround the letters we want

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the name, the possessive and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A critic praises Salman Rushdie for writing well on the subject of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in the possessive is ignored, so the S joins the letters on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is a heavy fuel oil burned in compression-ignition engines, which drive lorries, trains and generators.

clue.text: [See preamble]

blocks.note: the entry has no clue of its own
the preamble says every other solution is wholly or partly this, so it is found from the theme

explanation.walkthrough: Every other answer contains or is a measure or keeper of time, such as HOURIS, SECOND, ERA in IN CAMERA and EON in COME ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Clocks, watches, referees and conductors all mark or regulate the passing of hours and minutes.

clue.text: Strong shock when heart's bypassed in power cut

indicators.note: a bypass routes around the central part, leaving the middle out

blocks.note: outrage is a strong feeling of shock and anger
R is the central letter of the seven

explanation.surface: A heart patient gets a nasty jolt when the electricity fails during surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart's bypassed' sounds like cardiac surgery; here the heart is the middle letter of the shock word, which is skipped.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a period when the electricity supply fails, which is exactly what a power cut means.

clue.text: Like bad jokes, limited supply left to crack

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means bendily, so the letters bend into a new order
to crack something is to break it up, so its letters fall apart and regroup

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Bad jokes are like a limited stock left over for anyone who wants to crack them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun meaning stock, but it is the adverb from supple; 'crack' pairs with jokes in the surface yet also signals the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gag told at the wrong moment falls flat, so poor jokes are often ones delivered at an inappropriate time.

clue.text: Current changeover

indicators.note: to turn something over flips it, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: read as two words, change then over: to change a text is to edit it, and the second half is the turning signal

explanation.surface: A switchover is happening at the present moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changeover' looks like one word but splits into 'change' and 'over'. 'Current' is not the adjective for present but a flow of sea water.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide is the regular flow of the sea in and out, a current driven by the moon; the word also means a season, as in Christmastide.

clue.text: English bird is circling moor for endless periods

indicators.note: circling something means going all round it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a tern is a seabird
taken as written
to moor a boat is to tie it up

explanation.surface: An English bird circles over the moorland for what seems like forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like the open upland where birds fly, but it is the verb for securing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternity is a time without end, so the plural names spans of infinite duration.

clue.text: 8, for instance, discussed vetoed editorials

definitions.note: the definition says the answer is an example of 8, TIMEKEEPERS

indicators.note: what is discussed is talked about, so it is the spoken form that counts

blocks.note: vetoed means banned, and leaders are newspaper editorials

explanation.surface: Censored newspaper opinion pieces get talked about at length.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader is the British name for a newspaper's main editorial. The answer's link to 8 is that bandleaders beat time for their players.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor or bandleader sets the tempo for the musicians, so is one example of a keeper of the beat.

clue.text: Does regular income protect royal widows?

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it on all sides, so other pieces go inside

blocks.note: does is the plural of do, as in hairdos and parties; here it simply gives the verb
wages are regular payments for work
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A question: does a steady allowance keep the widowed queens comfortable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal widows' looks like a single definition, but 'royal' is the letter R inside the wordplay, leaving 'widows' alone to define. 'Does' gives DO, as in 'that will do'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow who holds a title or property inherited from her late husband.

clue.text: A politician is furious defending riots

indicators.note: defenders stand round what they guard, so the outer piece encloses the inner

blocks.note: to rage is to be furious
taken as written
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An angry politician speaks up for people causing disorder in the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb phrase 'is furious' supplies the outer piece, which wraps the A and the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently and destructively, much as a mob does when it riots.

clue.text: Big shop stocks an assortment of iron keys

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed selection, so the letters come out jumbled
to stock goods is to keep them inside the premises, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: M&S, Marks and Spencer, is a large British department store chain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large hardware store carries a range of iron keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keys' look like door keys in a hardware shop, but they are musical keys. Marks and Spencer is commonly shortened to M&S.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is a musical key built on the minor scale, such as A minor or D minor.

clue.text: Old gardener's extremely lonely in flat

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those are kept
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a flat surface is even
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An elderly gardener feels very lonely living in his apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' suggests an apartment but means level. John Evelyn was a 17th-century English diarist who wrote on gardening and trees.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn wrote Sylva and laid out celebrated gardens, so he is remembered as a historical horticulturist.

clue.text: Teams got rid of injured wings, perhaps

blocks.note: a team is a side
to wipe something off is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: Football teams dropped their injured wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings' look like football wingers next to 'teams', but they are the British word for a car's body panels over the wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that is sideswiped is struck along its flank, so its panels over the wheels are typically damaged.

clue.text: Assess writer's lost property

indicators.note: what is lost is no longer there, so those letters drop out

blocks.note: to assess a value is to estimate it
the writer's way of saying 'I am' is I'm

explanation.surface: An insurer values the things an author has mislaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost property' reads as a single phrase, but 'lost' is the instruction and 'property' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is land or possessions owned by someone, especially a large house with its grounds.

clue.text: Anybody swimming anonymously doesn't board

definitions.note: the definition is a verb phrase; the answer is a noun for one who does this

indicators.note: acting anonymously means without a name, so the letter for name is dropped
letters that are swimming move about freely and settle in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nobody who swims without being named gets on the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name, so 'anonymously' removes it. 'Board' looks like getting on a ship but means living in at school.
explanation.definitionFit: At a British boarding school, a day boy is a pupil who goes home each evening rather than living in.

clue.text: It's touch and go

blocks.note: first meaning: to affect someone's feelings
second meaning: a turn in a game, as in 'your go'

explanation.surface: Something is precarious, its outcome uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch and go' is an idiom for a risky situation, but here the two words are split into separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sad film can stir someone emotionally, and in chess or a board game each player's turn is called this.

clue.text: John Gay's overly evident in Amazing Grace

indicators.note: something amazing leaves one bewildered, and bewildered letters lose their order
what is evident in something shows up inside it, so one piece sits within

blocks.note: OTT is over the top, excessive
taken as written

explanation.surface: The poet John Gay's sentimentality shows too plainly in the hymn Amazing Grace.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gay was a poet, but read 'john' as slang for a toilet and 'gay' as a gay man: in British slang cottaging is gay men seeking sex in public toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word for a gay man who frequents public lavatories, which American slang calls johns.

clue.text: Peer into the unknown twice per annum

indicators.note: going into something puts it inside, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, used here two times
an earl is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller gazes into the future two times a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer into the unknown' reads as looking ahead, but 'Peer' is a nobleman, and the algebraic unknowns are x, y and z.
explanation.definitionFit: Per annum is Latin for each year, so it means happening once every twelve months.

clue.text: Jock's cross, forgetting Latin work by Juvenal, say

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so that letter goes missing

blocks.note: the saltire, a diagonal white cross on blue, is Scotland's flag; Jock is slang for a Scot
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is annoyed at forgetting his Latin while reading the Roman poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is the X-shaped flag. Jock is a British nickname for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenal was a Roman poet famed for his Satires, verse that mocks the vices of Roman society.

clue.text: Hurry to develop a proposal for it

blocks.note: first meaning: a call urging someone to get a move on
second meaning: to progress or improve, as a pupil's playing does
third meaning: a flirtatious invitation, with 'it' meaning sex

explanation.surface: A rush to work up a business plan for the project.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition. 'It' is the crossword's coy word for sex, so the proposal is a seductive advance.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation it urges haste, as a phrasal verb it means making progress, and as a noun it names a flirtatious advance.
